description: We are a passionate team of undergraduate IT students from Sri Lanka interested in space exploration, science, and technology. Our skills include software development, AI/ML, data science, web development, and problem-solving. We love turning creative ideas into innovative solutions. We welcome enthusiastic members with interests in astronomy, engineering, data analysis, UI/UX design, and scientific research. Let's collaborate, learn, and create something impactful using NASA's open data!
summary:
DeepSpace Doc is an autonomous, hands-free clinical co-pilot and medical access management system engineered for long-duration human spaceflight where Earth communication delays make real-time telemedicine impossible. 

We developed an Earth-independent emergency medical platform featuring bidirectional, hands-free "Live Voice assistance", 3D anatomical patient models, and microgravity clinical protocol retrieval (RAG) coupled with offline local fallbacks. Crucially, the system enforces "deterministic safety rails"  that cross-check patient allergies, drug–drug interactions, and real-time shipboard medical inventory before any treatment is recommended. To address the tension between rapid emergency care and astronaut medical confidentiality, DeepSpace Doc introduces an audited "1-tap biometric face-scan walk-up access" protocol and time-limited break-glass workflows with tamper-evident SHA-256 logging.

This project is vital for deep-space exploration: it empowers non-physician astronauts to confidently triage critical medical events within seconds while ensuring complete patient privacy and mission-control accountability.
details:
Project Details: DeepSpace Doc

1. What does it do or how does it work?

DeepSpace Doc is an autonomous, hands-free medical decision-support and emergency access platform designed for microgravity exploration environments (Lunar Gateway, Mars transit, deep-space habitats) where Earth communications latency of up to 22 minutes precludes real-time telemedicine. Operating alongside it is AEGIS-BIO, our specialized biomedical analytics and machine learning pipeline that monitors long-term physiological deterioration and environmental risk factors.

The system integrates four distinct operational workflows:

Instant Walk-Up Triage with Biometric Audit: In an acute crisis, unauthenticated crew members tap "Is there an emergency?" on the home screen. A 1-tap inline webcam biometric scan verifies identity, computes an SHA-256 integrity hash, stores the snapshot in the MongoDB audit log, and issues a 30-minute scoped emergency session without password barriers.

Hands-Free Bidirectional Live Voice & RAG Engine: The DeepSpace Doc Live voice assistant streams low-latency bidirectional native audio using the Gemini Multimodal Live API. It operates over a 15-protocol RAG library (microgravity CPR, burns, trauma, DCS) with an automatic offline local fallback.

Deterministic Clinical Safety Interceptors: LLM outputs are governed by deterministic safety code cross-checking the active patient's medical records (allergies, medications, baseline vitals) against real-time shipboard inventory (46 tracked items).

AEGIS-BIO Predictive Biomedical Pipeline:

Bone Mineral Density (BMD) Scan Analysis: Processes repeated bone-density scans comparing baseline with follow-up scans using the 95% Least Significant Change (LSC) threshold to reliably distinguish genuine bone loss from scan variability.

Cabin Co2 Forecasting Model: Predicts cabin Co2 levels one hour ahead from current Co2, active workout counts, cabin temperature, humidity, and time of day using StandardScaler + Ridge Regression.

Bone-Loss Classifier & Countermeasure Simulator: Evaluates whether simulated bone-region loss exceeds the 95% LSC threshold using a Random Forest model, projecting countermeasure trajectories over long-duration spaceflight.

2. AEGIS-BIO Pipeline Results & Biomedical Validations

A. Representative Bone-Scan Case Study — Subject 1392

[Figure 1: Subject 1392: BMD Change and Region-Specific LSC_95]

Figure 1 Analysis (BMD Change vs. Region-Specific LSC 95): The pipeline evaluates anatomical regions against individual precision error bands (+/-LSC 95 gray bands). Non-weight-bearing control (Forearm Radius/Ulna) exhibited +0.21% change, well within its +/- 3.06% noise band (grey dot). In contrast, the high-risk Femoral Neck dropped by -2.4%, substantially exceeding the -1.2% LSC 95 threshold (red dot), confirming genuine microgravity-induced bone demineralization beyond measurement noise.

B. Cabin Co2 Predictive Forecasting Model

[Figure 2: Cabin CO2: Actual vs. One-Hour-Ahead Forecast (Chronological Test Block)]

Figure 2 Analysis (Cabin Co2 1-Hour-Ahead Ridge Forecast): Time-series evaluation over consecutive mission days (11-25 through 11-28) demonstrating Ridge regression forecast tracking (dashed orange) against actual cabin Co2 partial pressure in mmHg (solid blue). The model anticipates operational spikes driven by crew exercise workouts and circadian diurnal shifts with high temporal accuracy (R^2 \approx - 0.85MAE approx 0.086 mmHg).

C. Machine Learning Model Evaluation Benchmarks

[Figure 3: Pipeline Model Evaluation (Values from Saved Metrics)]

Figure 3 Analysis (Model Performance Comparison):

Co2 Regression (Top & Bottom Left): Test R^2 = 0.850 (vs. persistence test baseline of 0.721); Test MAE = 0.086 mmHg (vs. persistence baseline 0.112 mmHg); Test RMSE = 0.135 mmHg (vs. persistence baseline 0.185 mmHg).

Bone Loss Classifier (Bottom Right): Training vs. Test vs. 3-Fold Grouped CV across Accuracy 81%train / 72% test / 76% CV), Balanced Accuracy (87% train / 83% test / 79% CV), and F1 Score (0.74 train / 0.55 test / 0.66 CV).

[Figure 4: Bone Classifier vs. Majority-Class Baseline]

Figure 4 Analysis (Bone Classifier vs. Majority Baseline): Grouped holdout testing demonstrates that while the majority-class baseline yields trivial 0.500 balanced accuracy, the AEGIS-BIO Random Forest classifier delivers 83.3% balanced accuracy (0.833), successfully detecting all positive bone loss cases exceeding the LSC 95 boundary.

D. Longitudinal Mission Countermeasure Simulation

[Figure 5: Simulated Femoral-Neck T-Score Across Mission Scenarios]

Figure 5 Analysis (Longitudinal Countermeasure Trajectory Projection): 36-month deep-space transit simulation comparing femoral-neck T-scores:

Unmitigated (Red): Steeper microgravity bone mineral loss crosses the warning threshold (T = -1.5) at month 20 and critical osteopenia threshold (T = -2.5) by month 34.

ARED Mechanical Resistance (Blue): Daily high-load resistive exercise slows bone loss significantly, keeping the T-score above -0.35 through month 36.

Bisphosphonate + ARED Combined (Green): Pharmacological antiresorptive therapy paired with physical loading maintains a stable bone density plateau (T approx +0.25) across the entire multi-year mission.

3. What benefits does it have?

Dual Acute & Chronic Coverage: DeepSpace Doc addresses immediate life-or-death emergencies within seconds (hands-free voice triage, anaphylaxis, cardiac arrest), while AEGIS-BIO monitors chronic mission risks (progressive osteopenia, sub-acute cabin hypercapnia, exercise countermeasure efficacy).

Hands-Free Microgravity Operation: Voice interaction enables uninterrupted clinical intervention during zero-G procedures while wearing sterile gloves or stabilizing a restrained patient.

Elimination of Medication & Supply Traps: Prevents contraindicated drug administration (e.g., Aspirin in allergic patients, Nitroglycerin with ACE inhibitors) and warns against out-of-stock items (redirecting to available ampoules).

Transparent Statistical Thresholds: Using calculated 95% LSC noise boundaries prevents false alarms in bone-density monitoring, ensuring countermeasures are prescribed only when bone demineralization is statistically authentic.

4. What is the intended impact of the project?

For exploration-class missions to the Moon and Mars with 4–6 crew members and a solitary medical officer, DeepSpace Doc and AEGIS-BIO minimize preventable morbidity, reduce mission-abort risks, and provide a self-sufficient clinical architecture that operates autonomously without ground-control telemetry dependencies.

5. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Frontend & System Architecture: Next.js 16 (App Router & Turbopack), React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS (Liquid Glass / Vision-OS design system).

Biomedical & ML Modeling (AEGIS-BIO): Python, Scikit-Learn (StandardScaler, Ridge, RandomForestClassifier), Matplotlib, Seaborn, Pandas, NumPy for 95% LSC statistical evaluation, chronological split time-series CV, and grouped stratified holdout validation.

Real-Time Voice & RAG: Google Gemini Multimodal Live API (gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview) for bidirectional voice and function calling (consult_emergency_protocol); Weaviate vector database for semantic retrieval over NASA-adapted protocols; OpenAI GPT-4o-mini & local JSONL fallbacks.

3D Visualization: Three.js and GLTFLoader for interactive 3D anatomical modeling and real-time physiological vitals mapping.

Persistence & Security: MongoDB (profiles, inventory, append-only logs), Node.js crypto (SHA-256 forensic hashing), HTML5 WebRTC/Canvas for biometric frame acquisition.

6. How is your project creative?

Ethical Emergency Break-Glass: Bridges the gap between astronaut medical privacy and urgent care through a 1-tap inline biometric face-scan that unlocks immediate emergency guidance while logging an immutable audit record for Earth-based flight surgeons.

Dynamic Cross-Crew Voice Lookups: Medics can treat one astronaut while verbally querying another crewmate’s allergies, medications, or fit-for-duty status over the voice loop, with the AI dynamically resolving and auditing cross-profile lookups.

Holistic Spaceflight Medicine Spectrum: Integrates microgravity acute trauma protocols (CMRS chest compressions, zero-G fluid management) with long-term predictive models (Co2 spikes and regional skeletal deconditioning).

7. What factors did your team consider? (Limitations & Future Work)

Distinction Between Simulation and Clinical Validation: We explicitly recognize that our ML models (the Co2 forecaster and bone classifier) represent trained prototypes developed on synthetic and initial sample sets. They demonstrate pipeline feasibility and evaluation workflows rather than final clinical validation.

Auditability & Traceability: All clinical decision support, model versions, evaluation metrics, and biometric access events are appended to audit trails with SHA-256 verification.

Future Work:

  • Validate Co2 predictive modeling against extended operational space station telemetry.
  • Train the bone classifier on expanded clinical cohorts with longitudinal dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) and quantitative CT datasets.
  • Report full predictive uncertainty intervals, sensitivity/specificity tradeoffs, and false-positive risk profiles alongside recommendations.
